title: Stream cohort kernel stitching and policy synthesis for graph consistency
text:
Stream cohort kernel stitching and policy synthesis for graph consistency

description:
Reduce non-deterministic capture failures and replay mismatches for concurrent decode streams by introducing a lightweight kernel probing and stitching policy that selects compatible kernel variants per stream cohort and enforces prefill fencing epochs.

background:
We see intermittent replay correctness failures when concurrent decodes use different kernel variants for the same logical operator (e.g., fused-attention vs. split-attention) across capture and replay boundaries. Existing mitigations (global kernel locks, full recapture) either harm throughput or increase latency dramatically during high concurrency. This ticket explores a middle-ground: identify stream cohorts with compatible kernel fingerprints at capture time and synthesize a stitching policy that binds kernels deterministically while allowing per-cohort variance.

proposal:
Implement a two-phase runtime: (1) at prefill/capture the runtime probes per-operator kernel fingerprints (fast lightweight exec on shadow inputs) and computes a cohort compatibility signature; (2) generate a stitching policy that pins kernel variants for the cohort and injects a minimal fence epoch when cohort boundaries change. On replay, the runtime validates fingerprint parity; if mismatch, fallback to a targeted recapture of affected segments rather than whole-graph recapture.

design_decisions:
Use shadow-probe runs on a subset of layers (first 2 attention blocks and the final attention) to compute kernel fingerprint instead of full-model probing
Represent fingerprints as 64-bit hashes of kernel metadata + small stat summary (seq len, head dims) to keep probes cheap
Cohort formation is opportunistic: streams with identical fingerprints within a 50ms window become a cohort
Fence epochs are lightweight CUDA stream barriers inserted only at prefill boundaries, not between every op
On mismatch, perform stripe-recapture: recapture only the graph segments that involve mismatched kernel variants
Policy prioritized for latency-sensitive routes: prefer kernel variants that minimize critical-path latency where cohort sizes are small

experiment_results:
Microbenchmarks on A100-80GB with 8 concurrent streams: cohort stitching reduced full-graph recaptures from ~18/hour to ~1.6/hour in stress tests
P99 decode latency change: +1.2ms on average due to probe overhead for single-stream, but -11% p99 under 8-stream concurrency because we avoid full recapture stalls
Token throughput improved by 6% in mixed-length workloads due to fewer global kernel locks
Failure reproduction: prior failure mode 'mismatch-after-prefill' was eliminated in 96% of synthetic repro cases using stripe-recapture fallback

acceptance_criteria:
Reduce full-graph recapture rate by >= 80% under 8x concurrent streams in synthetic stress test
No increase in error-rate (numerical divergences) attributable to stitching policy beyond baseline
Latency SLOs: p99 increase for single-stream workloads <= 2ms due to probes
Stripe-recapture fallback succeeds without causing full-graph recapture in >= 90% of mismatch cases

test_plan:
Unit tests for fingerprint hash stability across host builds
Integration test: 8/16 concurrent streams with randomized model shapes, verify recapture counts and end-to-end correctness
Chaos test: force kernel scheduler to pick different variants during capture and replay and verify stripe-recapture correctness
Benchmark: measure probe overhead and end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency across instance types (A100, H100, L4)

blockers:
Need ABI-stable kernel metadata interface from kernel selection team (PR 2 in flight)
Instrumented telemetry for cohort formation isn't fully integrated into Console yet
Corner-case: different quantization codepaths produce same metadata hash; need micro-stat check (means more probe work)

comments:
2026-02-10 Asha Patel (creator): Initial triage: reproduced mismatch-on-replay using small repro harness. Decided to explore cohort-based approach to avoid global locks.
2026-02-12 Liam O'Connor: Spike complete - shadow probes are cheap (~0.2ms per probe) on A100; will restrict to 3 layers for first pass.
2026-02-16 Design review (Marta Ruiz): Approved approach with one change: make cohort window configurable per-instance class. Added requirement to surface metrics in Console.
2026-02-20 Eng review (Kenji Yamamoto): Raised concern about hash collisions for half-precision kernels; added micro-stat checks (sampled output checksum) to probe plan.
2026-02-24 QA (Priya Singh): Synthetic stress run results attached; stripe-recapture avoided full recapture in 96% cases. Noted isolated hang in prefill fence insertion on older drivers.
